Q: Will future windows server OS support Asp Classic? A:

Officially, Microsoft has not set a specific End-of-Life (EOL) date for ASP Classic. Instead, its support is directly tied to the lifecycle of the Windows Server or Windows OS version it runs on.

As long as your version of Windows or Windows Server is still officially supported, ASP Classic (via IIS) remains supported.

However, keep these two critical factors in mind:

  • The Deprecation of VBScript: Microsoft is phasing VBScript (the primary language for ASP Classic) out of Windows. By around 2027, it will be disabled by default, and it will eventually be removed entirely in a future Windows release. Once fully removed, VBScript-based ASP Classic apps will no longer run natively.

  • OS Lifecycle Limit: While ASP Classic still works on Windows Server 2022 and 2025, its lifespan is limited to the support window of those operating systems (typically up to 10 years from their release).

Summary: While there is no sudden cutoff date, the upcoming permanent removal of VBScript after 2027 makes migrating to modern platforms like ASP.NET Core highly recommended.

Q: Flutter Linux desktop build fails with "No provider of glBlitFramebuffer found" after updating to Flutter 3.44.6 A:

This looks like an OpenGL compatibility issue rather than a Flutter build problem. The app is building correctly, but the Linux renderer is failing because your GPU/driver does not provide the required OpenGL features (glBlitFramebuffer).

Try checking your OpenGL support with:

glxinfo | grep "OpenGL"

Make sure you have updated Mesa/OpenGL drivers installed. You can also try running Flutter with software rendering:

flutter run -d linux --enable-software-rendering

If that works, it confirms the issue is related to GPU drivers or older hardware support. The Dell E4310 has older graphics hardware, so newer Flutter versions may require features that your current driver cannot provide.

Q: How to disable specific suggestions from appearing in message tab, but keep them inline in Visual Studio 2019 A:

Simply change the severity of the specific Code, for example IDE0090, from Default to Silent/None or open the .editorconfig file and then add the related command like

IDE0090: Use 'new(...)'

dotnet_diagnostic.IDE0090.severity = silent

will disable/hide the suggestions in the error list.

You mentioned you want to keep them when you are in files, does it mean that the suggestions disappear in Error List but still appear when you click the bulb in source codes? Not sure whether set the severity to silent could meet your requirement. If not, then I think this is not possible, as the severity is set for the analyzer and all prompt areas use and display the information from the same analyzer, also there is no other option to choose to display or not display the specific message.

Q: How can I (as the app developer) get notified when a user leaves a review of my app on Google Workspace Marketplace? A:

There isn't one. Nothing in the Marketplace SDK or the Cloud console, still true in 2026. You can reply to reviews but Google never tells you they exist.

Your options are polling the listing page yourself on a schedule and diffing the reviews, or using a service. Disclosure: I built one for my own add-on : Notify, it emails you when a new review lands.

Q: Trouble making Task Scheduler run my VBScript A:

This is a classic issue with COM automation (Excel, in this case) running under Task Scheduler with no one logged in. Even with Visible = False, Excel can still hang waiting on a dialog you'll never see — a file lock warning, a macro security prompt, stuff like that. I'd start by switching the task to "Run only when user is logged on" just to rule that out first.

Also, right now if Workbooks.Open or xlApp.Run fails for any reason, you get nothing back except a generic non-zero exit code in the Task Scheduler history — no idea what actually went wrong. Worth adding some basic error handling and logging so you can actually see where it's failing:

Dim xlApp, xlBook  
On Error Resume Next  
  
Set xlApp = CreateObject("Excel.Application")  
xlApp.Visible = False  
xlApp.DisplayAlerts = False  
xlApp.AutomationSecurity = 1 ' skip macro warning prompt  
  
Set xlBook = xlApp.Workbooks.Open("C:\Users\Todd Harris\Desktop\Monthly Calibration Report.xlsm", 0, True)  
If Err.Number <> 0 Then  
    LogError "Failed to open workbook: " & Err.Description  
    WScript.Quit 1  
End If  
  
xlApp.Run "CopyDatesAndEmail"  
If Err.Number <> 0 Then  
    LogError "Macro failed: " & Err.Description  
End If  
  
xlBook.Close False  
xlApp.Quit  
Set xlBook = Nothing  
Set xlApp = Nothing  
  
Sub LogError(msg)  
    Dim fso, ts  
    Set fso = CreateObject("Scripting.FileSystemObject")  
    Set ts = fso.OpenTextFile("C:\Users\Todd Harris\Desktop\vbs_log.txt", 8, True)  
    ts.WriteLine Now & " - " & msg  
    ts.Close  
End Sub

That'll at least tell you where it's dying instead of just "nothing happens." Also worth double checking in Task Scheduler that "Start in" is pointed at the script's folder, and that the account running the task actually has permission to open that file and launch Excel — I've seen this exact combo (works fine manually, silently fails scheduled) come from a locked-down service account more than once.

Q: How to create JWT token in Symfony5? A:

I think it may be because you have to add the jwt provider in the providers section in your security.yml :

providers:
  jwt:
    lexic_jwt: ~

If you are still stuck after this, I have implemented the Lexic JWT token in a project, so if you want an example you can check this out : https://github.com/niko-38500/boilerplate-symfony-hexagonal-architecture-CQRS-JWT

The class that generates the JWT token is located under "App\FrameworkInfrastructure\Infrastructure\Jwt\JwtGenerator", so you can follow the execution from there with a breakpoint to check if you notice any difference with your application which could help you.
